A Memorable Camembert, but an Overcooked Steak
Aug 2026 • Solo
Grilled Normandy Camembert — The Camembert was soft and creamy, and I thought grilling it really improved the overall flavor and texture. I also liked the touch of truffle honey, which added some sweetness that complemented the richness of the cheese. This was actually my first time trying Camembert, and I really enjoyed it.

Angus Grass-Fed Striploin — I asked for medium-rare, but the steak came out closer to medium. Because of this, it wasn’t as tender as I expected. The exterior had a nicely browned crust, though, and the steak still had a good beefy flavor. The sauce complemented and enhanced the meat, while the baby gem wedge added a nice crunch and, through its dressing, some acidity that helped balance the richness of the steak.

Good table
Dec 2025 • Couples
Stoker stands out as a serious and accepted address for quality meat lovers. The menu, which is very educational, details the cuts, the methods of cooking over a wood fire and the principle of dry-aging, reflecting a real culture of the product and an appreciable transparency.
The piece served, an impressive tomahawk with remarkable wigging, is presented raw at the table, on a board stamped, before cooking. A simple but effective ritual that inspires confidence. Cooking, precisely, was perfectly controlled, respecting to the letter the degree requested and fully enhancing the quality of the meat.
Important point to note for European customers: vegetables and starches are not included with meat, as is often the practice in Belgium. We must not forget to order them as an accompaniment.
The service is quality, attentive and professional, with good advice on both pieces and cooking or accompaniments. The whole gives the impression of mastery and consistency: here, meat is clearly at the center of the experience.
However, prices are high for Vietnam, but consistent with the positioning, product quality and level of service offered.
A convincing address for lovers of beautiful pieces, provided you accept the budget.

Nice Setting and Service - But Steaks Fell Short
Jul 2025 • Family
I had high hopes for our dinner at Stoker Woodfired Grill & Bar in Ho Chi Minh City. With its strong ratings on TripAdvisor and a mention in the Michelin Guide, it was one of the few restaurants I had marked as a must-visit on our trip to Vietnam. The space itself is warm and stylish, with a modern, upscale ambiance that immediately set the tone for what we expected to be a memorable steakhouse experience.

The bread service was a surprising standout—beautifully baked, flavorful, and served warm. A clear 5/5.

For starters, we tried the Wagyu Beef Tartare, which was beautifully plated and absolutely delicious. Another strong 5/5.

Unfortunately, the mains - the steaks - left us underwhelmed, especially for a restaurant that brands itself around wood-fired grilling.

- The grain-fed ribeye my son ordered had a nice char and good flavor overall. However, he requested medium rare, but it arrived clearly rare. Still enjoyable, but a miss on execution. (4/5)
- I ordered the grass-fed ribeye, asking for rare plus. It came out closer to medium, with no discernible char and surprisingly little flavor. It lacked the depth and smokiness you'd expect from a wood-fired steak. (1/5)
- My daughter ordered the filet, medium rare, but it arrived more medium, and was unfortunately bland. It was so underwhelming that she didn’t even want to finish it. (1/5)

When you go to a steakhouse, you expect the steaks to be the hero of the meal, unfortunately for our experience they were the weakest part. It was disappointing, especially given the restaurant’s reputation and premium pricing.

Out of this world flavors
Jan 2024 • Couples
It was by far the best 3 courses of meals I have had in my life. 

We were having a hard time choosing a place for our final dinner of Ho Chi Minh so we opted for the Michelin filter and moved forward. A bad stomach flu from local food led us to this steakhouse.

The bone marrow and tartar as startera were great. I am a fan of beef tartar and it was very likely the best I have had, anywhere.
Main course duck breast was amazing and the portion was big (2 breasts opposed to the 1 we get in Europe normally), but the star was the Wagyu beef. Paired with the chimicurri sauce and pinches of salt it was like an explosion of flavour and texture in my mouth. It was by far the most unbelieveable piece of beef I have eaten. The recommended sides of potato puree and asparagus were spot on.
The cheesecake and meringue dessert were amazing.

The recommended wine pairings by the server for each course were absolutely spot on.

For the prices you get absolutely top notch quality in the food, the atmosphere and the serving. We came in as walk-ins at 6.30 and were gladly seated, the restaurant filled to full over time.
